productionVerification: Nothing under packages/ changes in this PR, so merging it triggers no Release Packages run; the production `Push version bump` step with the new push-main can only be observed on the next Release Packages run (any package). A same-package race — the `Resolving the packages/<dir>/package.json version-line conflict to v<version>` line followed by a green push — needs two releases of one package to land close together; that is the implementer's post-merge production check.
observations: Outside the five acceptance lines, for the architect/reviewer: when origin is unreachable (remote path does not exist), `git push` fails and then `git fetch origin main` fails under `set -e`, so push-main exits 128 with git's `fatal: … does not appear to be a git repository` and no `::error::`/job-summary line. The plan's global constraint says every push-main failure should state the release succeeded; this path does not. Pre-existing behaviour (the old script had the same shape), low likelihood in Actions (GitHub unreachable mid-step), deterministic to reproduce: `git remote add origin /nonexistent.git` then `release-push.sh push-main packages/pkg 1.0.1` → EXIT=128. Not a failing verdict on any acceptance line; naming it so nobody reads exit 128 as covered.

The release itself succeeded: …`, rebase aborted (no rebase-merge/rebase-apply dir, `git status` clean of rebase), origin/main tip and manifest (1.0.0) untouched.
